Who we are looking for
The Head of Enterprise Architecture owns the target-state design of the technology estate and the standards, patterns and governance through which it is realised . This is the architectural blueprint that determines how every platform, application and integration in the firm is built, connected, secured and retired.

The mandate is to reduce complexity while increasing optionality — cutting technical debt, rationalising a fragmented estate, and establishing the reusable architectural foundations that let engineering teams move faster within known-good boundaries. Success is measured not in documents published but in estate outcomes: fewer bespoke solutions, faster architectural decisions, demonstrably lower run cost, and an architecture capable of absorbing the pace of change that Frontier AI and post-quantum cryptography will impose.

A central element of this mandate is establishing the architecture that makes the firm AI-forward — the compute, serving, integration and control foundations on which AI becomes a governed production capability rather than a portfolio of experiments. This is delivered in deliberate partnership with the Head of Data & AI, who owns model strategy, data products and AI delivery.

This is a deeply technical leadership role . The successful candidate is a credible principal-level architect who has personally designed systems at scale, and who will lead through technical authority rather than positional mandate — equally effective authoring a reference architecture, defending a standard to a skeptical business-unit CIO, and presenting an estate rationalization case to the Senior Leadership.

Why this role is Important to us
- Architecture is an enabling layer, not a gate. Governance exists to accelerate good decisions, not to inspect bad ones after the fact. If review is the bottleneck, the pattern library has failed.
- Patterns over permissions. The fastest, cheapest, pre-approved way to build is to use an existing pattern. Teams may deviate through a time-boxed, registered exception — and inherit the support and compliance burden of doing so.
- Reduce before you add. Every new pattern admitted to the library should retire something. Complexity is the primary long-term cost driver of the estate.
- Serve the whole estate. Mainframe, vendor-package, analytics and quant populations receive proportionate patterns and standards. An architecture that governs only greenfield services has failed.
- Cost is an architectural property. Spend, unit economics and run cost are designed in, not discovered in the invoice — including the economics of accelerated compute and inference.
- Complementary, not overlapping. Where a peer function owns a domain — Data & AI, Cyber, Developer Platforms — EA owns the interfaces, standards and cross-domain coherence, not the delivery.

THE 4 BIGGEST BLOCKCHAIN STRENGTHS ARE ALSO ITS WEAKNESS

 - Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

 - Decentralization leads to too many standards https://xkcd.com/927/

 - Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

 - Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.




BLOCKCHAINS ARE OPTIMIZED FOR WRITES, NOT READS. 

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases https://x.com/Tim_Roughgarden/status/1512847113599729668. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

 - Fragmented standards

 - Exponential complexity

 - No accountability for interpretation

 - Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.




ALLIUM IS BUILDING THE SYSTEM OF RECORD FOR ONCHAIN FINANCE

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

 - Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

 - Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

 - Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

 - Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.




FINANCE IS MOVING ONCHAIN

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously https://x.com/AlliumLabs/status/2019810793324482901?s=20, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability. 

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

----------------

Most people with treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, or OCD spend years cycling through medications before anyone mentions there are other options. Treatments like accelerated TMS, SAINT, Spravato, and IV ketamine can work when nothing else has. They're also hard to find, hard to get covered, and hard to deliver well. That gap is why Radial exists.

We support the country's largest network of brain medicine clinics: 27 clinics and more than 100 clinicians across seven states, caring for patients with some of the most serious mental health conditions there are. RadialOS, our AI-native operating system, matches patients to the right treatment, coordinates their care, and takes administrative work off clinicians' plates. **Job Description Summary**
===========================

As part of the GE Aerospace Digital Technology organization supporting the Defense & Systems (D&S) business, the Director of DevOps, Support, and Operations keeps the Defense and Systems Customer Experience (DSCX) application portfolio secure, reliable, and compliant. This is a people-leadership role accountable for vulnerability remediation, reliability (SLA, SLO, and SLI), automation and toil reduction, vendor management, defect management, legacy lifecycle and sunsetting, and resilience and continuity including on-call and disaster recovery. This person will lead a team of operations and application engineers and set the operational discipline for the portfolio.

**Job Description**
===================

**Why This Role Exists**

DSCX owns 30+ digital products for Defense & Systems. Today our technical product managers wear three hats for their products: product management, project management, and operations. We are dividing that load across three dedicated functions, and this role will build out the operations discipline, consolidating ticket management, software hygiene, patching, and vulnerability closure into a single team. This role is planned to have 6-8 direct reports, and the portfolio includes many legacy applications and reports that need to be retired, rewritten, or absorbed into our AI product vision. Vulnerability and high priority defect findings come from the Defense & Systems security organization under the BISO, and closing them inside the severity SLA, including CMMC obligations on affected products, is part of this team's accountability. Your charge is to standardize processes and artifacts, build automation that removes the manual work, and then coach and train your team to hold it. You should be experienced with AI and know where it creates opportunity to expand what the team can deliver.

**Environment**

The DSCX portfolio runs primarily on AWS, Palantir Foundry, or through SaaS based 3rd party solutions, with on-premise implementations supported for customers whose data sensitivity requires it. Delivery runs through Rally and Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow is our system of record for incident, change, and defect management. Monitoring and alerting tooling varies by application across the portfolio, and consolidating it is part of this team's work. Finally, the portfolio carries a $25+MM annual budget across our product line.

**Roles and Responsibilities**  
  
**Security and Vulnerability Remediation**

* Own vulnerability remediation and high-priority application defects across the DSCX portfolio, working against the policy, scanning cadence, and severity SLAs set by the Defense & Systems Business Information Security Officer (BISO), who is the source for both.
* Accountable for getting DSCX applications compliant against the BISO's D&S-wide program, including CMMC obligations on affected products.
* Own the remediation backlog with a named owner and target date

Founded in 2015 to develop the world’s first industrially scalable laser metal additive manufacturing solution, VulcanForms is reshaping how the world manufactures critical products. Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

===============

Orbis is hiring a Vice President of Engineering to lead our engineering organization through its most significant period of growth. You will lead our engineering directors and managers, hire and develop an exceptional technical workforce, and shape a culture where engineers do their best work while the organization triples in size over the next year.

You will report directly to the CTO and serve as the senior engineering leader accountable for how Orbis builds: the people, the leaders, the culture, the delivery engine, and the engineering standards. The CTO sets technical vision and architecture direction; you own the organization and operating model that turns that vision into reliable delivery at scale.

This role is built for a leader who has done it before in a small, fast-moving company, and who can bring structure without bureaucracy. You will be a visible, trusted voice with engineers, executives, and government customers alike. Our engineers work remotely across the United States and its territories, including Puerto Rico, so building ways of working that span time zones is central to this role.

========================

* The market, the buyers, and every client problem worth solving

- Collaborating with other teams to drive business process improvements and program optimization

- Regular, consistent and punctual attendance. Must be able to work nights and weekends, variable schedule(s) as necessary.
- Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Employees at all levels are expected to:
- Understand our Operating Principles; make them the guidelines for how you do your job.

NVIDIA’s advanced datacenter boards push forward chip packaging, PCB fabrication, SMT, assembly, and testing capabilities. Dedicated teams take responsibility for each technology: packaging manages the package, PCB and materials handle fabrication and stack-up, SMT and assembly oversee build processes, and test and SI focus on test capabilities. The challenge is to align these improvements across the stack—from chip to PCB, PCB to SMT, SMT to assembly, and assembly to test. The Senior Director, Board PDE oversees integration methods that make this possible—coordinating handoffs, engineering cross-domain effects before changes, and optimizing the entire chain.

- Design, implement, and institutionalize the integration readiness process for all next-generation datacenter board products — owning manufacturing and test readiness end to end so build starts land on schedule and at target yield.
- Guide the functional teams in developing cross-boundary techniques before silicon and stackup freeze occurs. Focus on warpage-tolerant DFM and reflow for next-gen BGA pitch. Manage impedance and CTE control for high-speed stackups. Lock pad-map and fab methods at an early stage.
- Build, lead, and develop a global Board PDE organization across three technical pillars — PCB & Fab, SMT/PCBA, and High-Speed Connector & Signal Integrity.
- Set up integration oversight throughout the chip-to-board stack. Define entry and exit requirements at each domain boundary. Lead the gates to confirm one qualified domain is ready to pass to the next.
- Collaborate with Operations Test Engineering and Signal Integrity to establish test coverage and manufacturing test flow requirements, applying that thoroughness to the tester and diagnostic boards.

We are EnduroSat! A fast-growing space scale-up at the forefront of satellite innovation, specializing in advanced software-flexible satellites for commercial, governmental, and scientific endeavors.

* **This is more than a job, it's a mission**

  We are making space universally accessible and redefining the possible
* **We get things done**

  We take ownership of what we do and we work hard to make a difference
* **We are fearless**

  Transpаrancy is our only way forward. We dare to address and resolve issues head-on

**What is the role?**

As our VP of Engineering & Chief Engineer, you will own the final technical delivery of EnduroSat US across hundreds of missions and the engineering organization that creates it. Systems engineering, mechanical, structural and FEA, thermal, software, and the other disciplines all report to you. You hold final technical authority on US programs: you decide what the system looks like, you sign off on the final architecture, and you are accountable when it does not work.  
  
The engineering problem here is not clean-sheet design. Our satellites share a common platform, and the value we deliver is the last mile on top of it — the integration, and mission-specific design that turns a proven bus into a spacecraft that does a particular customer's job. You will assess whether our existing system design can meet a given mission, decide where it must change, and conceive adapted or new capability where it cannot. That takes deeper judgment than drawing from scratch, because every decision must survive contact with a platform, a schedule, and a supply chain that already exist.  
  
You will be in front of customers regularly — large commercial, civil, and defense organizations whose engineering teams will test whether our answers hold up. You will shape mission concepts during capture, defend architectures at PDR and CDR, and make requirements less dumb. You need the depth to take final decisions yourself and exceptional focus to ignore the noise so a mission can achieve what it needs on time and on budget, not the perfect solution that never comes.  
  
You will work as a peer to our VP of Mission & Programs, who owns delivery and the program relationship. You own what we build and whether it will work; they own getting it delivered and flown. You will also be in close contact with the European technological leadership who own the platform you are building on — keeping US and European engineering aligned on standards, architecture, and interfaces is part of this job, not an afterthought.  
This role is based in Los Angeles and is primarily on-site, with travel to customers and to our European headquarters. You will report to C-level management.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Head of Production to join our team in Santa Ana, CA to stand up a cutting-edge manufacturing site. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will build and lead the product line organization from scratch, establishing and managing manufacturing processes, quality systems, and the infrastructure needed to scale from prototype builds through full-rate production.

As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must bear the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Your spectrum of support will be exceptionally diverse and require you to rapidly drive aggressive deliverables to completion.

The ideal candidate will leverage a deep expertise in large-scale manufacturing of a number of large, complex assemblies. You need to have experience in heavy fabrication, be able to lead the complex integration of different structures, and have a background spanning structural fabrication, joining and assembly across a variety of metals, alloys, and exotic materials. You need to have led an organization of hundreds, not dozens, and come from an operation comparable to the scale we are building at Anduril. You are a builder, not a caretaker.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Own all production activity: manufacturing and production support.
- Build and lead the production organization, supporting hiring across manufacturing engineering, quality, and operations.
- Establish manufacturing processes and production infrastructure for complex electromechanical vehicles.
- Drive NPI and the manufacturing development lifecycle: Concept, Prototype, LRIP, FRP.
- Manage production budgets, schedules, and on-time delivery performance.

Pendo's Data Platform is the backbone of everything we do. Our systems process more than 50 billion events per day, peaking at over 1 million events per second, and manage dozens of petabytes of data across several production environments. - Lead multiple engineering teams responsible for our real-time data ingestion pipeline, analytics batch job pipelines, and analytics query engine — setting technical direction and roadmap while balancing near-term delivery with long-term scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency.

The North Tarrant Express (NTE) was the first design-build-finance-operate-maintain managed lanes project in Texas and consisted of the complete reconstruction of 13.3 miles of the existing I-820/SH-183 corridor between Dallas and Fort Worth. Since opening in October 2014, nine months ahead of the contracted completion date, the general highway lanes are experiencing a 70% decrease in congestion time and a 15% increase in average speed. This Cintra-led project has doubled capacity and significantly improved mobility along this heavily congested corridor that traverses the heart of six cities through Northeast Tarrant County.

The project is operated and maintained by the Cintra-led consortium in North Texas. This project has improved mobility by adding additional road capacity through a combination of general highway lanes and continuous frontage roads, along with tolled express lanes that use variable pricing to keep traffic moving.

Since opening in September 2015, the general highway lanes are realizing a 60% decrease in congestion time and a 10% increase in average speed.

As Director of Data Science & Analytics, you will build and lead the team that turns Coherent's manufacturing, supply chain, and commercial data into better decisions. You will set the analytics strategy, deliver production machine learning, and partner with operations, engineering, finance, and sales leaders. Your work will directly improve yield, capacity planning, cost, and speed to market as we scale output for AI infrastructure customers.

- Set the strategy. Define and run Coherent's data science and analytics roadmap. Tie every initiative to business goals and track its measurable return.

Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own Crux's relationships with the governments, communities, and public audiences that decide where and how fast Crux can build. Data centers today earn their permits, tax agreements, and utility approvals in rooms full of neighbors, county commissioners, and school boards, and increasingly in state legislatures, public utility commissions, and the press, and schedule risk concentrates there. Your job is to make Crux the developer that communities and governments say yes to, and to keep that yes durable through a multi-year build. You will build this function from zero: the government affairs strategy, the community engagement playbook, the community investment program, the corporate communications rhythm, and the relationships at every level of government and at every site in the pipeline. The role works hand-in-hand with site selection, entitlements, energy, construction, operations, and executive leadership.



In this role, you will:

 - Lead Crux's government affairs strategy at the local, state, and federal levels: build relationships with elected officials, agency and regulatory staff, and economic development agencies, and track and shape the policy issues that affect data center development, including energy and interconnection, water, tax incentives, and permitting.

 - Build and maintain relationships with the stakeholders who decide our projects' fate, including county and municipal officials, planning and zoning staff, utilities, school districts, business organizations, and community non-profits, in every market Crux enters.

 - Serve as Crux's external affairs lead and spokesperson, representing the company with policymakers, trade associations, industry coalitions, and the media, and advise executive leadership on emerging political, regulatory, and reputational issues.

 - Own the company-level communications narrative and manage the PR agency relationship: set priorities, direct agency work, and coordinate closely with executive leadership, legal, and Blackstone/Google partner teams on major company updates such as financings, partnerships, site announcements, and leadership news, so that Crux speaks with one consistent voice.

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. We introduced precision medicine to the world and built an industry around the idea that every patient deserves answers as unique as their DNA. **Job Summary**:

The Director of Quality Assurance leads the QA organization through its transformation to an AI-optimized SDLC, able to support multiple product launches and continuous feature delivery in parallel across a multi-tenant SaaS platform. This leader defines the overarching quality strategy, champions the integration of AI tools across the entire SDLC, and scales automated, resilient testing frameworks to accelerate delivery while sustaining the reliability and regulatory compliance Medrio's customers depend on. This position reports directly to the SVP of Engineering and works closely with Development, Product, Support, and Compliance throughout the SDLC. The QA organization is geographically dispersed, combining onshore and offshore teams of in-house engineers and external vendor partners working across multiple time zones.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* **AI-Driven Quality Strategy:** Lead the strategic integration of generative and predictive AI tools throughout the SDLC, including AI-assisted test case creation, requirements analysis, and automated risk-based test coverage.
* **Quality Throughput & Capacity:** Scale quality output in line with an AI-accelerated development organization, ensuring test capacity keeps pace with development output without compromising quality. Success is measured through cycle time to release, escaped defect rate, automated test coverage, and full regression suite runtime.
* **Modern Test Automation Leadership:** Oversee the evolution of automated testing strategies for a multi-tenant SaaS platform, prioritizing modern frameworks like Playwright alongside AI-powered self-healing test infrastructure to minimize script maintenance and maximize suite reliability. This includes tenant isolation and data-segregation testing, configuration-driven test matrices across tenant variants, and management of shared-schema regression risk.
* **Organization Oversight:** Direct all activities of the QA organization, ensuring continuous validation, high platform stability, and alignment with modern quality engineering best practices.
* **Regulatory & Compliance Quality:** Ensure QA practices, documentation, and evidence meet the requirements of a regulated healthcare environment (including HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11, GxP/CSV, SOC 2, and GDPR where applicable), and support internal and customer audits as a senior representative of the quality function.
* **Validation of AI-Generated Test Assets:** Own the framework by which AI-assisted test artifacts are reviewed, approved, and evidenced, ensuring automation generated with AI meets the traceability and audit standards required in a validated environment.
* **Security-Forward Quality:** Partner with Security and DevOps to embed security testing into the delivery pipeline (SAST/DAST, dependency and vulnerability triage, and coordination of penetration testing), and ensure PHI is appropriately handled and de-identified across test environments and test data.

For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid, bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.

The Power Applications team takes power orchestration algorithms from idea to production. The Opportunity
Philanthropy has long operated with fragmented data, duplicative processes, and systems that do not easily speak to one another. The Philanthropy Data Commons (PDC) was created to change that.

By enabling information to move securely across the systems that organizations already use, the PDC can reduce the repetitive administrative burden on nonprofits, help changemakers gain greater visibility to aligned funders, and give them greater control over how their information is shared, while giving funders a clearer view of organizations, needs, and funding flows.

The PDC has moved well beyond an idea. With significant foundational work completed, including a live Exchange application, an evolving governance framework, a growing network of funders and ecosystem participants, and more than 20 organizations committed to sharing data, PDC is entering an important period of transition and growth.

The focus now is on expanding participation, demonstrating the value of shared data at greater scale, and building the coalition that can make PDC an enduring part of how philanthropy works.

The inaugural Executive Director will have a rare chance to help shape the next stage of the initiative and a broader shift in the field. They will build on significant investment and momentum while helping the PDC grow its reach, deepen its partnerships, strengthen its financial sustainability, and establish its long-term organizational home.

At a time when advances in AI are making access to trusted, well-governed data increasingly important, the PDC has the potential to become essential infrastructure for a more connected, informed, and effective philanthropic sector. For an entrepreneurial leader energized by building in ambiguity, this is a chance to take years of investment and a powerful sector-wide idea and turn it into something enduring, shaping not only the future of the PDC but how philanthropy shares and uses data.

Conceptualized in 2021, the Philanthropy Data Commons is a collaborative initiative temporarily hosted by Mac Services, Inc. that connects the systems, organizations, and data that philanthropy runs on. It provides a shared infrastructure that allows funders, changemakers, and the ecosystem partners they already use to share information on their own terms.

About Helion

We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone.

Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion.

This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait.

Every Helion fusion pulse runs current through semiconductor switches operated well beyond commercial ratings. Our next generation of fusion machines requires devices designed for our circuits rather than adapted to them, gated devices integrated as multi-die modules, and packaging that survives repetitive high-energy pulsing for power plant-scale lifetimes. You will lead the team that delivers these, from device physics through a development-scale fabrication capability to pilot module assembly and test, and you will carry it into high-volume production with external fabrication partners. Your team’s work will help determine how reliably Helion’s power plants operate, how frequently they can pulse, and how effectively we can manufacture and deploy future plants.

 - Establish and lead partnerships with high-volume fabrication facilities so that devices developed in-house transfer cleanly to production at scale. Continue to develop Helion's existing device vendor relationships

Now we're scaling it to thousands of tonnes of annual production.

 


THE ROLE

Head of Engineering will lead Solcoa's Engineering team with the goal of developing and scaling up novel rare earth metal production processes. You will own a full metal production development program. This includes development starting from research, process development, and full scale reactor design. You will also own the engineering, construction, and commissioning of Solcoa’s first commercial facility.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Process Design. Own the design of the metal production process that will bring metal production to cost parity with China. In this capacity, you will identify bottlenecks and radically simplify Solcoa’s process.

 - Reactor Design. You will lead the design and engineering of the modular high-temperature metallothermic reduction reactors capable of producing rare earths at high yield and high throughput. You will organize the research, simulations, and mechanical engineering teams for the engineering and fabrication of it.

 - Solcoa One, Process Design. You will identify key requirements, milestones, and be responsible for the delivery of the operating process at Solcoa One, our first commercial metal production plant. Head of Engineering will lead the process engineering team, responsible for designing the process and balancing of the plant. You will work with the Head of Capital Projects to engineer, staff, commission, and ramp up the largest rare earth metal production plant in the United States.

 - Organization. You will define weekly goals and long-term milestones for the individual contributors on the research team, process development team, and mechanical engineering team. You will identify hiring needs and capital budget needs for achieving the metal capacity goals set by Solcoa’s leadership. You participate in the major decisions that define the direction of Solcoa’s metal production business.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary.

 - Generous stock options.

 - Comprehensive medical, dental and vision insurance.

 - Company-provided lunch daily.

 - Visa sponsorship available if needed.

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

-
Coach and develop engineers and 3+ engineering managers

-
Create an inclusive team culture, recruit for, and retain extraordinary engineering talent

-
Be a thought leader in coming up with long term technical strategy tightly coupled with business needs

-
Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

-
5+ years of engineering management experience leading cross-functional teams, especially in building complex web and mobile products

-
2+ years of experience managing engineering managers

-
1+ years of experience closely managing iOS or Android engineers

-
Proven strategic technical leadership and an ability to make sound technical decisions across complex initiatives

-
Experience navigating complex product organizations and balancing diverse stakeholder requirements

-
Experience with fostering healthy feedback environments

-
Demonstrated track record of inspiring, coaching, and developing high-performing engineering leaders and teams

-
Familiarity operating in a high-pressure, fast-paced

In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Role Overview

Role:

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Resilience Engineering & Operations to lead our Resilience Engineering and Operations team in Bothell, Washington. In this role, you will lead the team responsible for keeping IonQ's hosted quantum computers running reliably for customers, while improving resilience, performance, throughput and operational efficiency across the fleet.

This is a technical leadership role, not a purely administrative one. You will lead a team of Operating Physicists, engage credibly with complex trapped ion systems, and use sound judgement to balance uptime, technical risk and long term improvement. You will work closely with engineering, physics and operations partners, and your team's insight will help shape how current and future systems are supported in the field.

You will also play an important part in building our follow the sun operating model alongside colleagues in Europe. The function is still maturing, so this role needs someone comfortable building process, improving handoffs and creating clarity in a fast moving environment.

Responsibilities:

In this position, you will lead day to day fleet support, incident response, operational readiness and continuous improvement for IonQ's hosted quantum systems, as well as installation and maintenance of our internal systems at the College Park office. You will set direction for the team, support individual growth, and make sure the group can respond effectively to both immediate operational issues and longer term reliability challenges.

You will work at the intersection of operations, engineering and physics, helping the team resolve complex issues, strengthen fleet performance and feed operational learning back into future designs, tooling and automation. Early on, you will put durable operating processes, metrics and prioritisation habit

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most by challenging norms and fixing the ER experience. * A bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field

Specializing in water, energy, and waste management, Veolia Group designs and implements innovative solutions for decarbonization, depollution, and resource regeneration, supporting communities and industries in their ecological transformation. - Lead the vision, strategy, and execution of the process engineering function in support of Water Tech NORAM integrated growth objectives.

**PURPOSE**

The Director of Applied Innovation leads the team that builds, deploys, and runs Central Valley Ag's custom business applications — products such as RouteForge and Gravis, the grower portal, and the applications that follow them. This is a working leadership role. The Director sets direction, develops the team, and also writes code, reviews it, and carries the hardest problems personally.

The team is small on purpose and fast on purpose. It uses AI-assisted development as a normal part of how work gets done, and it is measured on working software in the hands of CVA employees and growers — not on documents, roadmaps, or demonstrations. The Director is accountable for the availability of every application in the portfolio, for the experience of the people who use them, and for equipping CVA's support organization to carry routine support over time.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of two: an Applied Innovation Engineer and an Applied Innovation Analyst. Hire into the team as it grows.
* Personally design, develop, and review application code. This position ships.
* Own the application portfolio roadmap. Run intake with business leaders, set priorities against business value, and decide what the team will not build.
* Establish and hold a delivery cadence that puts usable software in front of users in weeks rather than quarters, and report against it.
* Own production availability for the portfolio: deployment, release management, monitoring, and incident response.
* Establish and enforce engineering practice — version control, testing, code review, release and change management, and documentation.
* Establish the team's AI-assisted development practice: tooling, review standards, guardrails, and the appropriate handling of company and customer data.
* Partner with Enterprise Architecture so that applications conform to CVA's architecture, integration, and data standards.
* Partner with IT Infrastructure and IT Security on hosting, identity, access management, and secure development practice.
* Equip CVA's support organization to support business applications: build the documentation, runbooks, training, and knowledge transfer that let tier 1 and tier 2 support be carried outside this team. Serve as the escalation point.
* Hold the boundary with the data organization: Applied Innovation builds the operational applications that run the business, while tools and agents whose purpose is answering questions from CVA's data belong to the Director of Data & AI Enablement. Partner with that team rather than duplicating it.
* Manage vendor relationships, cloud spend, and licensing for the application portfolio.
* Report delivery, risk, and portfolio health to the Chief Technology Officer and to business leadership.
